newsitem.title: USA: Fruehauf names new president, forms committee.
newsitem.headline: Fruehauf names new president, forms committee.

text.p: Fruehauf Trailer Corp. said Friday that Derek Nagle, executive vice president of its North American operations, was named president of the company, which has been struggling to reduce its debt.
Nagle will assume most of the responsibilities previously held by Thomas Roller, who resigned as president and chief executive Aug. 20 to assume those positions at Wolverine Tube Inc.
Fruehauf, which makes truck trailers, also said that Timothy Wiggins, executive vice president and chief financial officer, resigned, effective Sept. 15, to accept a new position.
The company, based in Indianapolis, also said its board formed a special committee to coordinate the implementation of a previously announced strategic plan to reduce debt.
Richard Nevins, a director of the company since January 1995, will chair that committee.

Nevins said the board was pleased that Nagle agreed to accept the responsibilities of president. "He is the best possible person to provide the leadership the company needs at this time," Nevins said.
Earlier this month Fruehauf said it was pursuing several alternatives to reduce is debt burden, including the possible sale of one or more units, or the entire company.

For the second quarter Fruehauf posted net income of $5.7 million, or 15 cents a share, including a $14 million gain on the sale of overseas assets. Excluding the sales, it would have had a net loss of $8.2 million, or 21 cents a share.
Fruehauf's stock was unchanged at 62.5 cents in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
